articleTitle: Can soft-starters help save energy?
abstract: Electric motors, which are predominantly of the three-phase, induction, squirrel-cage type, consume about 60% of the electrical energy generated in industrialized countries [1]. In many cases, a motor runs on full load for only a small fraction of the operating time. Often, motors are so much overrated with respect to the actual load that they never utilize their full power capabilities. Average efficiency of such drive systems is inferior, since the motors, like all electric apparatus, are designed to operate most efficiently when fully loaded. There are two basic approaches to the minimization of energy consumption by ac drives. One possibility is to employ an inverter that adjusts both the supply frequency and the voltage, so that the motor speed can be controlled and the energy usage reduced [2], However, many applications do not require the expensive frequency control, and motors can be equipped with power electronic soft-starters instead. The supply frequency is fixed and only the stator voltage is controlled, in dependence on the load, to limit the stator current at starting and reduce the motor losses [3-5].

articleTitle: The origins of 60-Hz as a power frequency
abstract: In 1891, Westinghouse engineers in Pittsburgh selected 60 Hz as their new power frequency. That same year, AEG engineers in Berlin selected 50 Hz as their new power frequency. Although much has happened since 1891, these two frequencies remain the principal power frequencies in use worldwide.

articleTitle: Motor insulation system quality for IGBT drives
abstract: Prior to the introduction of insulated gate bipolar transistor (IGBT) switching devices, the main issue motor designers were concerned with in mating a motor to an adjustable speed drive (ASD) was the increase in temperature rise from the harmonic losses the ASD introduced [1].

articleTitle: Induction motor drives for domestic appliances
abstract: Simplicity and robustness make the three- phase induction motor attractive for use in domestic appliances, including washing machines. The simple structure of the rotor and absence of the brush gear permit a high rotor speed, enabling a high power to be obtained from a given motor frame size. A variable-frequency, variable voltage supply from an inverter allows operation over a wide range of speeds.

articleTitle: Reliability analysis of emergency and standby power systems
abstract: Different facilities have varying requirements for reliability of electric power supply. Even at the same facility, various loads may have different reliability requirements. Some loads, such as medical facilities, emergency lighting, data processing, and chemical process industries, are very sensitive to interruptions in electric supply. Standby and emergency power systems [1,2,3] are installed at such premises to provide electric power of acceptable quality.

articleTitle: The historical development of neutral grounding practices
abstract: John Dunki-Jacobs is guest author this month, recounting his views on the history of neutral-grounding practices. Dunki, as he is widely known, is eminently qualified for this task. He is a Fellow in the IEEE and recipient of the Richard Harold Kaufmann Field Award and the IEEE Medal for Engineering Excellence. Dunki continues an active career devoted to the development of and contributions to the engineering and implementation of industrial power systems. His career encompasses most of the important developments in industrial power systems occurring in the time following World War II.—ELO

articleTitle: Testing and performance of transformer differential relays
abstract: The phenomenon of transformer magnetizing inrush current has been discussed in many-papers throughout the years [1-7]. In 1958, the complexity and characteristics of single-phase versus three-phase banks were discussed in detail [1], A brief review of magnetizing inrush follows to provide the basis of need for transient testing.

articleTitle: Pressure sensor performance and reliability
abstract: Pressure sensor devices are used to monitor the performance characteristics of various systems within the appliance industry. The household washing machine has long employed sensor devices to monitor and control the tub water level during fill cycles. These devices have evolved from early waterweight or float switches to rubber diaphragm mechanical-type devices [1]. The development of epoxy packaging capability for silicon sensors, improved die bonding material, and reliability testing results indicate that the silicon piezo-resistive transducer (PRT) promises to be the next plateau.

articleTitle: Origin, development, and design of K-factor transformers
abstract: In 1987, the University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee held a seminar in Scottsdale, Ariz., where I was one of the speakers covering, among other things, the effect of transients and surges on the primary windings of transformers of medium voltage ratings, 5 KV to 15 KV.

articleTitle: Quality and reliability of energy efficient motors
abstract: Even though the stage has been set for energy conservation being one of the major drivers in the design of general-purpose industrial motors, it was not intended to be at the expense of reliability or the overall motor performance. Some have felt that the drive for increased efficiency would diminish motor life and performance. This article is based on a review of various industrial motors available.

articleTitle: Applying energy-efficient motors in the petrochemical industry
abstract: Several U.S. and Canadian utilities have implemented demand side management (DSM) programs for retrofitting energy efficient (EE) motors. This article examines some of the practical problems associated with this [1-6].

articleTitle: A comparison of light sources for the petrochemical industry
abstract: Presently, the calibration of photometers is based on the spectral sensitivity of the eye with the field of view limited to only 2 degrees. However, lighting applications of interest in work environments are rarely confined to such small fractions of the visual field. New research shows that the eye spectral sensitivity is different when a full field of view is considered. The changes in spectral sensitivity in full field are due to the influence of rod photoreceptors which have been previously and erroneously viewed as being responsive only at extremely low light levels. The rod or scotopic response has been found to be the primary spectral response of the pupil at multiple light levels, varying from typical interior levels to lower outdoor levels, such as those found in a petrochemical facility at night. In addition, scotopically rich sources impact brightness perception.

articleTitle: History
abstract: The February series of IEEE board meetings has just concluded. All six boards (Technical Activities, Regional Activities, Standards, Education, Publication, and U.S. Activities) as well as the IEEE Board of Directors (BOD) met and conducted the business at hand. As a general observation, the IEEE is alive and well.

IEEE Keywords: IEEE Center for the History of Electrical Engineering

articleTitle: Turbidity sensing as a building block for smart appliances
abstract: The U.S. Department of Energy standards for laundry and dishwashers are expected to be announced soon for appliances built after Jan. 1,1999- To meet these high-efficiency targets, the OEM designers are searching for practical solutions to improve the efficiency of these appliances. The availability of turbidity sensing on appliances will provide design engineers with a way to determine how soiled a particular load of clothes or dishes may be so engineers can then create a control system that adapts the operation of the machine to save water, time, and energy, while providing superior cleaning performance. Because of this capability, the turbidity sensor is emerging as a key building block developing the next generation of energy-efficient “smart” appliances.

articleTitle: Short circuit protection of energy efficient motors
abstract: More than 30 years ago the molded case circuit breaker industry developed a line of motor short circuit protective devices or “instantaneous trip breakers” that improved on the thermal magnetic or “inverse time breaker” in two distinct ways. First, the instantaneous only breaker (sometimes called a motor circuit protector) had no long time or “thermal trip.” It was deemed redundant since the overload relay or “heater” was providing this long-time thermal function.

articleTitle: Design aspects and performance of a slotless PM motor for hard disk drives
abstract: The trend in magnetic hard disk data storage systems is increased capacity with a reduction in form factor. Increasing storage capacity essentially means packing more disks, using smaller heads and higher co-ercivity media. The actuator systems in the hard disk drives (HDDs), the spindle and the voice coil actuator will have to meet with the new demands. The spindle motor will have to provide higher starting torques due to the increased number of heads and disks. This is contrasted by the reduction in form factors and reduced current specifications. A 5.25-inch HDD has typical starting and running currents of 4 A and 2 A, respectively, while a 2.5-inch HDD is allowed to draw less than 900 mA and 80 mA, respectively [1, 2]. (It is the usual practice in the disk drive industry to use inches for certain quantities.)

articleTitle: Sensorless switched reluctance starter/generator performance
abstract: A switched reluctance machine based system, whether a motor drive or a starter/generator, requires the rotor position to be determined in order to commutate at the correct instants. Resolvers are used especially in high-speed systems, or sometimes encoders in lower-speed systems, to obtain rotor position. However, resolvers are expensive, and both resolvers and encoders are a source of single point failure. This article compares the performance of a highspeed switched reluctance starter/generator (SRS/G) system when operating with a resolver to that when operating resolverless, or sensorless.

articleTitle: A unique cogeneration application in a large pulp mill electrical system
abstract: Recently, Canadian utilities have begun investigating the viability of independent power producers, providing generation facilities to operate in parallel with the utility systems. Cogeneration in industrial plants is often an excellent source of such generation. In the case described in this article, it was determined that two 48.7 MVA, 13.8 kV, 0.84 pf, 3600 RPM steam turbo-generators would be the most Economical method of power supply for the 1500 Adt/d green field pulp mill.

articleTitle: Reliability of lightning-resistant overhead lines
abstract: Lightning continues to be the major cause of outages on overhead power distribution lines. Through laboratory testing and field observations and measurements, the properties of a lightning stroke and its effects on electrical distribution system components are fairly well-understood phenomena [1]· A meticulous compilation of 32 years of historical records has been kept for outage causes, duration, and locations for eight distribution feeders at the Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL). Due to the limited growth of ORNL, the number, length, and location of the 13.8 kV overhead lines have remained the same between I960 and 1992. Except for noted differences (voltage construction class, length, age, and maximum elevation above a reference level), other factors that could influence the reliability of an overhead line have remained nearly the same. This allowed a meaningful reliability study to be performed on the entire ORNL electrical distribution system [2].

articleTitle: Variable frequency drives for commercial laundry machines
abstract: Variable-speed ac drives have a well- founded reputation for versatility and dependability, with many features and benefits chat are just not available from other drive technologies. They are presently used in applications ranging from simple fan control to complex operations including process loops, positioning and indexing, and industrial laundry applications.

articleTitle: Recommendations in HV DC testing of MV cable insulation
abstract: Recent research and field reported data supports the theory that high voltage DC testing can reduce the life of both unaged and aged medium-voltage cross-linked polyethylene (XLPE) cable insulation. This research led an industry movement to eliminate factory DC testing, and reduce the field level and frequency of DC testing.

articleTitle: Failed motors: rewind or replace?
abstract: Most process users of electric motors have long recognized the economic wisdom of buying energy-efficient motors for use on new capital projects. It is known that the power cost savings of such motors compared to standard-efficiency models will generally pay for the price differential within the first several months of operation. The Energy Act of 1992 mandates that most types of commonly used motors manufactured as of October 1997 or later must be energy-efficient designs.

articleTitle: Short circuit currents of the SEPTA traction power distribution system
abstract: The Southeastern Pennsylvania Transportation Authority (SEPTA) is undertaking a multi-phase modernization program of various electrical and infrastructure facilities. In this effort, a considerable amount of the facilities will be upgraded or replaced. The electrical power supply system is planned to be upgraded with modern state-of-the-art equipment. The overall aim of this effort is to increase the system performance and reliability while maintaining passenger and operator safety.

articleTitle: Effects of coupling installation on motor performance
abstract: This article discusses the variety of couplings used; proper selection, installation, and alignment of the couplings; potential forces which might be generated by the couplings; and their effects on the motor bearings. The consequences of sustained external loads on the motor bearings will be addressed for both anti-friction and sleeve bearings. Specifically, the following topics will be addressed: □ Coupling selection □ Proper installation and alignment of couplings □ Forces generated ay couplings □ Effects of external forces on motor bearings

articleTitle: Evolution of induction motors-the ever-shrinking motor
abstract: The induction motor was invented in the 1880s by Nikola Tesla, and you might say it is basically unchanged 100 years later. But this is true only in the sense that you might say the automobile is unchanged during the same time period—same four wheels on rubber tires, some springs, a steering wheel, an engine. But what tremendous changes have occurred! One of the most notable changes is physical size. You might ask, “As motors continue to shrink, is it possible they will become vanishingly small?” We shall explore that question.

articleTitle: Optimum pole configuration of variable speed AC induction motors
abstract: Sometimes a user who is familiar with fixed- speed AC induction motors may specify a variable speed AC requirement with a preconception of the number of motor poles. This is appropriate in the case of an application where the motor will be run “across-the-line,” and is expected to run at the same speed and load as provided on inverter operation. If, on the other hand, “bypass” operation is not required, a more optimal choice of motor designs might be available.

articleTitle: Electrical Area Classification drawings: a comparison
abstract: This article will compare the types of Electrical Area Classification drawings that have been prepared for chemical and petroleum processes and highlight the differences and, in particular, the application variations of NFPA 497A and API RP500. It will discuss the complexities in applying these standards. Finally, it will present a technique that meets OSHA Process Safety Management requirements and has other significant advantages.

articleTitle: An intelligent ignition system
abstract: Electrical resistance ignitors (ERI) have gained wide acceptance during the past ten years as an ideal means of ignition for gas-burning appliances. The change from standing pilots has brought about many new direct burner ignition appliances. Electrical resistance ignition has proved to be more reliable than spark because of the relatively high ignition power available from a 120 or 240 volt line. This low voltage does not require the suppression circuitry needed with spark controls in order to reduce interference to the electronics now employed in most burner controls. Also, spark controls deliver high voltage to the electrodes (12,000 V or more), which may arc to other areas due to dirt, moisture, or eroded spark gaps, thus causing system shutdown.

articleTitle: Kraft continuous digester effective alkali control
abstract: Dynamic Modeling Technology (DMT) is a new approach for modeling process transfer functions, which reduces the effort required to obtain accurate process models. DMT is able to automatically determine the structure of the transfer function model as well as the values of the model parameters using an unstructured approach based on orthonormal Laguerre functions. DMT provides several advantages compared to classical S-Plane (Laplace Transform) frequency response methods such as the ability to easily model high order behavior and process dead time.

articleTitle: API 541 Third Edition: an improved purchasing specification [for electric motors]
abstract: The American Petroleum Institute (API) Standard 541, third edition, is a standard that covers the minimum requirements for form-wound coils, and squirrel cage rotor induction motors 250 horsepower and larger (this is generally above the NEMA 440 frame size). The purpose of this API 541 standard is to serve as a comprehensive purchasing specification that can be used by specifiers of high-performance motors. Although this specification is tailored to the needs of the petroleum industry, it can readily be applied by all industries. Users no longer have to prepare their own purchase specifications, and manufacturers can design and produce motors to a standard that will be widely accepted. Ultimately, repeated use and acceptance of this standard will result in higher-quality motors at competitive prices.

articleTitle: Time division multiplexed bus for machine control
abstract: From the early days of the 914 to today, adding features to our machines has been a major task of our business at Xerox. These features were required not only to remain competitive but also to improve copy quality and reduce field maintenance. This is true today and will be true in the future as well.

articleTitle: On-line utility tie power factor control
abstract: Large industrial operations with internal electrical generation capabilities and parallel utility ties have always worked to control watt and var flows across their tie lines. In today's economic climate, the ability to control tie line operation can significantly impact a facility's bottom line.

articleTitle: High interrupting capacity equipment for hazardous locations
abstract: There are numerous methods of handling high fault currents in the modern industrial facility. When it comes to hazardous locations, however, questions abound as to the equipment and systems required to survive these conditions without causing ignition of the surrounding atmosphere.

articleTitle: Engineering licenses are not for everyone
abstract: Licensure is not for you unless you’re looking for a credential that you can carry from job to job that will differentiate you from other applicants, that will demonstrate a commitment to engineering as your profession and your pride in your ability.

articleTitle: Characteristics of shaft voltage and bearing currents
abstract: Efficiency and productivity improvements attainable through adjustable speed operation of process lines, air handling systems, water treatment facilities, paper and metal lines placed ac adjustable speed drives (ASDs) at the forefront of motor control. Simultaneously, modern high frequency switching power devices, employing bipolar junction transistors (BJTs) and faster insulated gate bipolar transistors (IGBTs), have produced unintended consequences on peripheral equipment, generally described as electromagnetic interference (EMI).

articleTitle: A transfer function approach to harmonic filter design
abstract: This article details a new transfer function approach in passive harmonic filter design for industrial and commercial power system applications. Filter placement along with six common filter configurations are presented. Harmonic impedance, voltage division and current division transfer functions are derived and used in a practical filter design procedure that incorporates IEEE-519 distortion limits directly into the design and component specification process. A simple four-step filter design procedure is outlined and used in a variable speed motor drive pumping plant application.

articleTitle: High-speed electric drives: technology and opportunity
abstract: Until the mid-1980s, the load commutated synchronous inverter was the only viable option for medium-voltage, high-horsepower, electric adjustable speed control. Thus, synchronous motors made up the vast majority of all large, high-speed installations prior to I99O. The largest single application for these units was driving large boiler feedwater pumps in power generation sites. While some of these applications exist in the United States, Japanese and European companies have been far more aggressive in promoting the potential of this “new” technology, and most installations are outside North America. All totaled, there are more than 120 installations representing more than 2 million lip in the world for large (ranging from 3,600 hp to 55,000 hp) high-speed (greater than 3600 rpm) synchronous installations throughout the world. Some of these have been in operation for 15 years. Table 1 offers greater derail.

articleTitle: Elimination of supply harmonics
abstract: The price of the extensive use of power electronic devices is becoming clear: increasing harmonic “pollution.” The same switching conduct that allows active devices to perform with a proficiency that belies their size is responsible for supply harmonics generation. Since there is no viable alternative for these non-linear devices in electrical engineering, the subject of supply harmonics presently has broad interest. According to the Electric Power Research Institute (EPRI), presently “3540% of all electric power flows through electronic devices. This is supposed to increase to 60% by the year 2000” [1], Without a doubt, the source of potentially harmful harmonics is growing.

articleTitle: Protective relay application for generators and transformer
abstract: Application of overcurrent protective devices for generators and transformers is generally considered to be a routine task. However, a review of the protective device selection, device settings, and protection requirements for generators and transformers, as well as their connected buses, has revealed that certain lessons can be learned in examining a few typical applications. The applications are presented in a series of case studies. The case studies are in the following categories of protection problems: 1. Generator backup protection a. Bus-connected generators with feeder circuits at generator voltage b. Unit-connected generators with voltage restraint time-overcurrent relays (device 51V) for backup protection. c. Unit-connected generators with distance relays (device 21) for backup protection. 2. Transformer protection with high 3-phase fault currents and low-ratio current transformers a. Original protection scheme. b. Upgraded protection scheme.

articleTitle: Electro-forensic engineering: an emerging profession
abstract: With the increasing number of legal cases involving application of electrical equipment, forensic engineering is playing a greater role in providing litigation support. This article discusses the qualifications and role of the electro-forensic engineer. Safety practices, importance of codes and standards, and how to minimize accidents and liability are growing concerns with electrical equipment manufacturers, systems designers, contractors, and owners. The electro-forensic engineer can make positive contributions beyond litigation support as explained in this article. The need for recommended practices or standards for the electro-forensic engineer to perform in a professional manner is also discussed.

articleTitle: Justifying and planning an energy monitoring system
abstract: In order to stay healthy and competitive, businesses are using manufacturing metrics to help drive their goal of making profits in the most efficient way possible. When they are efficiently managed with power monitoring systems, electrical distribution systems can have a significant positive impact on many metrics. Monitoring systems, which many large companies are using success fully, can track energy usage within the plant, allocate costs, manage load, and collect information that can be used to identify equipment or operating problems. In addition, these systems can help reduce capital costs for power system expansion.

articleTitle: Upgrade of winders with AC drives and the synchronous rectifier
abstract: The purpose of a winder is to cut the paper arriving from a paper machine into strips of specific width and wind ir into a roll of definite diameter. Practical experience in the production of newsprint has shown that the maximum operating speed of a winder must be approximately 2.0–2.5 times the operating speed of the paper machine.

articleTitle: Proper specification and installation of induction motors
abstract: To achieve years of trouble-free operation, the proper motor for an application must be chosen. This requires that the motor be properly specified for the specific application, taking into account any special ambient conditions, performance requirements, or environmental concerns. Without this, nothing else will matter.

articleTitle: Vacuum retrofits: the process, benefits, and risks
abstract: Reliability has been defined by NASA as “the probability of a device performing adequately for the period of time intended under the operating conditions encountered” [1], Based on this definition, older circuit breakers have had an excellent reliability for the period of time intended.

articleTitle: One company's guideline for hazardous area classification
abstract: Historically, hazardous area classification has been the responsibility of the plant electrical engineer. In actuality, however, many projects were being designed with minimum input from plant engineering. Most consulting firms would use an ultra-conservative approach with little input from process engineers and no consideration for potential cost savings. The existing national standards and guidelines are written to provide safety and flexibility of design and are difficult for the inexperienced engineer to interpret. Even for the experienced engineers, this flexibility often leads to different interpretations for similar situations. In 1993 a small group of electrical engineers recognized a need for standardization without compromising safety, and formed a technical committee to address this issue. This paper will present the result of the committee's work as a corporate engineering technical guideline that is currently being used by Eli Lilly and Company.

articleTitle: 1996 Conference Award Highlights
abstract: Numerous outstanding achievements were recognized at the 1996 IAS Annual Meeting, held Oct. 6-10, 1996, at the Hotel del Coronado in San Diego, Calif. Congratulations to this year's recipients: 1996 Outstanding Achievement Award. The Society Outstanding Achievement Award honors a member who has made an outstanding contribunized with 10 prize paper awards. He has openly shared his knowledge in the more than 100 seminars he has presented throughout the country and in the IEEE severe-duty motor standards committees which he has served.

articleTitle: Sensorless Control Of AC Drives: Speed And Position Sensorless Operation [Book Review]
abstract: This book provides the state of the art in the already fast-expanding interdisciplinary (electrical machines and drives, automatic control, computer science) field of sensorless control of AC drives. Various papers published in IEEE transactions and conferences and in other international journals are carefully selected based upon new contributions to technological advances, practical feasibility, tutorial value, and applicability to speed or position sensorless operation. Four AC motors are discussed—induction motors, permanent magnet AC motors, synchronous reluctance motors, and switched reluctance motors, the book being organized into four sections. Each section begins with a resume of the main ideas presented in different selected papers.

articleTitle: Power Electronics And Variable Frequency Drives Technology And Applications [Book Reviews]
abstract: The new book by Bose was released by IEEE Press in August 1996. Unlike other books by Bose, this one is unique and contains 11 chapters, each of which was contributed by a world-renowned specialist in the respective area. Unlike a typical IEEE Press book, which contains preprinted papers from IEEE publications, this one is an originally contributed book. However, each chapter is essentially an expanded version of paper published in the Proceedings of the IEEE Special Issue on Power Electronics and Motion Control (August 1994). The book was sponsored by IEEE Industrial Electronics Society, the Industry Applications Society, and the Power Electronics Society.
